PART III  Nutrition in the Life Cycle
Vitamin D deficiency is recognized increasingly in dark-
skinned and veiled women living in latitudes where sun expo-
sure is low. Women who are at risk of entering pregnancy with 
low vitamin D levels also include those with BMI more than 30, 
those with fat malabsorption, and those with high use of sun-
block, along with poor dietary intake. Screening for vitamin D 
status is advised for those women (ACOG, 2011).
Severe vitamin D deficiency is associated with congenital 
rickets and newborn fractures and also may manifest as seizures 
(ACOG, 2011), although it is unknown if calcium insufficiency 
also plays a role (Brannon and Picciano, 2011). There is concern 
that low maternal vitamin D status may negatively affect fetal
